title: Help-centre search engine
issue: Users say search highlights look broken on words like "don't", and support noticed that identical FAQ entries come back in a different order after every re-index. The test suite is red.

bugs.summary: A token's end offset uses the normalised word length (apostrophes removed), so highlights and snippets cut words with apostrophes short.
bugs.symptom: The failing tests are in highlight.test.js and point at highlight.js, which is correct.
bugs.spec: README, Analysis: "start / end: character offsets of the original word in the original text, end exclusive (text.slice(start, end) is exactly the word as written, apostrophes included)".

bugs.visibility: visible only after the first fix (masked)
bugs.summary: Equal scores keep insertion order instead of being ordered by document id.
bugs.symptom: The FAQ test first checks the highlighted snippet (fails because of tokenizer.js) and only then the id order. A comment claims the stable sort makes this fine.
bugs.spec: README, Ranking: "equal scores are ordered by document id (ascending string order), so results and pages are stable no matter in which order documents were added".

bugs.summary: idf is ln((N − df + 0.5)/(df + 0.5)) instead of ln(1 + (N − df + 0.5)/(df + 0.5)); it goes negative for words in more than half the documents, which inverts their ranking.
bugs.symptom: Visible tests only compare the order of rare words, where both formulas agree.

distractors: stemmer.js TODO says "news" → "new" is too aggressive; the README documents it and a hidden test checks it
suggest.js TODO calls a correct early exit wrong
indexing.test.js indexes concurrently with varying delays and looks flaky; it is correct
query-parser.js TODO about OR/parentheses (out of scope by design)
